bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.

bill.title: High-Quality Charter Schools Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Hearings held.

industries.rationale: The bill directly subsidizes contributions to charter school organizations, expanding their funding sources and operational capacity.
The bill allows donations of market securities, which may affect how financial institutions handle charitable transfers of investment assets.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create a federal tax credit equal to 75% of cash or securities donated to eligible charter school organizations that create or expand charter schools. Individual taxpayers could claim up to $5,000 or 10% of their adjusted gross income, whichever is greater, with unused credits carried forward for five years. The bill sets a $5 billion annual cap on total credits, with $10 million allocated to each state and the remainder distributed first-come, first-served, and requires charter organizations to spend contributions within a specified timeframe or lose eligibility.

bill.latestActionText: Indefinitely postponed by Senate by Unanimous Consent.

industries.rationale: The bill would eliminate a fee charged to oil and gas companies for methane emissions above specified thresholds.
Some electric utilities operate natural gas systems that could be subject to the emissions charge this resolution would nullify.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify an Environmental Protection Agency rule published in November 2024. That rule established procedures for charging oil and gas companies an annual fee when their methane and other greenhouse gas emissions exceed certain thresholds. If enacted, the resolution would eliminate these compliance requirements and the associated emissions charge program.

bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
subjects: Hybrid, electric, and advanced technology vehicles

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects heavy-duty trucking by determining whether stricter California emission standards apply to commercial vehicles and engines.
The bill affects manufacturers of heavy-duty vehicles and engines by determining whether they must comply with California's stricter NOx emission requirements.
Stricter emission standards for heavy-duty vehicles could affect demand for diesel fuel and related petroleum products.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn an Environmental Protection Agency decision that allowed California to enforce stricter pollution standards for heavy-duty trucks and engines than federal law normally permits. The EPA had granted California a waiver to implement its "Omnibus Low NOx" regulation, which sets tougher limits on nitrogen oxide emissions from vehicles. If this resolution passes, that waiver would be nullified and California would be blocked from enforcing those stricter standards.

Zero-emission vehicle mandates affect demand for electric vehicle charging infrastructure and clean energy services for commercial fleets.

bill.title: Patients Deserve Price Tags Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 522.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services
Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new price-disclosure obligations on hospitals and surgical centers, changing their administrative and compliance requirements.
Medical device costs must be included in the price estimates, affecting how device manufacturers' products are priced and disclosed to patients.
Price transparency requirements may affect how insurers negotiate rates and how patients understand their coverage and out-of-pocket costs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, and other healthcare facilities to provide patients with upfront price estimates for scheduled procedures and services. The estimates would need to include costs for the facility, physicians, anesthesia, medical devices, and other associated charges. Facilities that fail to provide these price disclosures could face civil penalties.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

bill.title: Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects manufacturers and sellers of lead ammunition by limiting federal authority to regulate their products on public lands.
Manufacturers of fishing tackle containing lead would face fewer potential federal restrictions on their products' use.
Sporting goods retailers selling lead ammunition and tackle would benefit from reduced regulatory uncertainty around these product lines.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent three federal agencies—the Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Forest Service—from banning or regulating the use of lead ammunition or fishing tackle on federal lands and waters. The agencies could still impose restrictions in specific locations if they determine, based on field data from that site, that lead use is the primary cause of a wildlife population decline and the state agrees to the regulation. Certain existing regulations would remain in place.

plain.whoItTouches: People who live near or work on federal land.

bill.title: A bill to prohibit the award of Federal education funds to educational institutions and agencies that do not allow for religious exemptions to vaccination requirements, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates eligibility for federal education funding based on vaccination exemption policies at schools and universities.
Changes to vaccination requirement policies at educational institutions could affect demand for vaccines administered to students and staff.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit the federal government from awarding education funds to schools, colleges, and educational agencies that do not allow religious exemptions to their vaccination requirements. Educational institutions that wish to continue receiving federal funding would need to permit students and staff to claim religious exemptions from any vaccine mandates they impose.
